title: Cardinal Billing Account Term Payoff: Payoff Balance, Unbilled Premium and Prepayment Credit
content:
**Computation clause.** A term payoff on a Cardinal Billing Account is a single payment that the named insured makes from their own card or bank account through the automated payment line to pay the rest of the current term in advance; the part above the balance stays on the account as a credit that the installments still to come are drawn from, and because installment fees attach only to installments as they are invoiced, the payoff itself carries no installment fee. The term payoff is the posted payoff balance plus the premium still to be invoiced, less the prepayment credit. The posted payoff balance is every installment invoiced, fee charged, returned payment, additional-premium bill and refund posted on the account, less every payment, credit, fee waiver and write-off posted on it; the premium still to be invoiced is the term premium plus additional premium less return premium received for the term, less the premium of the installments already invoiced; the installments of the term are one plus the package's term months divided by the plan's installment interval, less one. The prepayment credit is the prepayment credit rate of 1.0 percent applied to the prepayment credit base, which is one even installment share of the premium still to be invoiced (that premium divided by the installments still to be invoiced), rounded to the cent once, as its final figure, no intermediate figure being rounded. The term payoff amount is rounded to the cent.

## Quantities

| Quantity | Definition |
|---|---|
| Posted payoff balance | Installments invoiced, fees charged, returned payments, additional-premium bills and refunds posted, less payments, credits, fee waivers and write-offs posted |
| Premium still to be invoiced | Term premium, plus additional premium, less return premium received for the term, less the premium of the installments already invoiced |
| Installments of the term | One plus the result of the package's term months divided by the plan's installment interval, less one |
| Installments still to be invoiced | Installments of the term less the installments of the term already invoiced |
| One even installment share | Premium still to be invoiced divided by the installments still to be invoiced |
| Prepayment credit | 1.0 percent of one even installment share, rounded to the cent |

The package's term months are those of the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy package the account bills; the installment interval is the pay plan's.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

A six-month term on a monthly plan has 6 installments; 4 have been invoiced, so 2 are still to be invoiced. The posted payoff balance is $180.00 and the premium still to be invoiced is $430.00.

1. One even installment share: $430.00 divided by 2, that is $215.00.
2. Prepayment credit: 1.0 percent of $215.00, that is $2.15.
3. Term payoff: $180.00 plus $430.00, less $2.15, that is $607.85.
